<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"/>
<title>The Exclusive-Dimension Ramp Explorer</title>
<style>
  :root{
    --bg:#0f1226; --panel:#181c39; --ink:#eef1ff; --muted:#a3aad6;
    --accent:#5ad1ff; --accent2:#ffd166; --bad:#ff6b8a; --good:#7bf1a8;
  }
  *{box-sizing:border-box}
  body{margin:0;background:linear-gradient(160deg,#0b0e20,#141936 60%,#0d1024);
       color:var(--ink);font-family:-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,"Segoe UI",Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;}
  .wrap{max-width:1080px;margin:0 auto;padding:26px 18px 48px}
  h1{font-size:1.55rem;margin:0 0 4px;letter-spacing:.2px}
  h2{font-size:1.05rem;margin:26px 0 10px;color:var(--accent)}
  p.lede{color:var(--muted);margin:0 0 18px;line-height:1.55}
  .grid{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 320px;gap:18px}
  @media (max-width:900px){.grid{grid-template-columns:1fr}}
  .panel{background:rgba(24,28,57,.85);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.08);
         border-radius:14px;padding:16px 18px;box-shadow:0 8px 30px rgba(0,0,0,.35)}
  canvas{width:100%;height:auto;display:block;border-radius:10px;background:#0c1024}
  label{display:block;font-size:.82rem;color:var(--muted);margin:14px 0 4px;
        text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.09em}
  input[type=range]{width:100%;accent-color:var(--accent)}
  .val{float:right;color:var(--accent2);font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}
  .readout{font-family:ui-monospace,SFMono-Regular,Menlo,monospace;font-size:.88rem;line-height:1.75}
  .readout b{color:var(--accent)}
  .pill{display:inline-block;padding:2px 9px;border-radius:999px;font-size:.75rem;
        background:rgba(90,209,255,.14);color:var(--accent);margin-right:6px}
  .seedrow{display:flex;gap:6px;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-top:8px}
  .seed{width:34px;height:34px;border-radius:8px;display:flex;align-items:center;
        justify-content:center;font-size:.8rem;font-weight:700;color:#0b0e20}
  .cure{background:var(--good)} .fail{background:var(--bad)}
  button{background:linear-gradient(180deg,#2d3672,#222a5c);color:var(--ink);
         border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.14);border-radius:9px;padding:9px 14px;
         font-size:.85rem;cursor:pointer;margin-top:12px}
  button:hover{border-color:var(--accent)}
  .note{color:var(--muted);font-size:.85rem;line-height:1.6;margin-top:10px}
  table{width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;font-size:.85rem;margin-top:8px}
  th,td{text-align:right;padding:4px 6px;border-bottom:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.07)}
  th:first-child,td:first-child{text-align:left}
  th{color:var(--muted);font-weight:600}
  code{background:rgba(255,255,255,.07);padding:1px 5px;border-radius:5px}
</style>
</head>
<body>
<div class="wrap">
  <h1>The Exclusive-Dimension Ramp Explorer</h1>
  <p class="lede">
    A boundary symbol reserves <b>k</b> private directions inside a space of dimension
    <b>n</b> over a field with <b>p</b> elements. The system has <b>m</b> degenerate
    ("obstruction") directions, and a run <em>fails</em> when all k private directions are
    swallowed by one of them. Drag the sliders: the reliability curve
    P<sub>cure</sub>(k) = 1 − P<sub>fail</sub>(k) is always a <em>ramp</em> pinned between
    p<sup>−k</sup> and m·p<sup>−k</sup> — monotone, sublinear, and
    never equal to 1.
  </p>

  <div class="grid">
    <div class="panel">
      <canvas id="plot" width="1300" height="720"></canvas>
      <div class="note">
        Blue: the exact single-obstruction curve 1 − p<sup>−k</sup>.
        Shaded band: the proved envelope for any obstruction family of size m.
        Dashed red: a hypothetical capacity cliff — the shape the mathematics rules out.
        Stars: the measured reliabilities 0.25, 0.33, 0.83, 1.00, 1.00 at k = 0, 1, 2, 4, 8.
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="panel">
      <label>characteristic p <span class="val" id="pv">2</span></label>
      <input id="p" type="range" min="2" max="11" step="1" value="2"/>
      <label>obstruction modes m <span class="val" id="mv">1</span></label>
      <input id="m" type="range" min="1" max="32" step="1" value="1"/>
      <label>ambient dimension n <span class="val" id="nv">24</span></label>
      <input id="n" type="range" min="4" max="192" step="1" value="24"/>
      <label>exclusive width k <span class="val" id="kv">1</span></label>
      <input id="k" type="range" min="0" max="16" step="1" value="1"/>

      <h2>At the selected width</h2>
      <div class="readout" id="out"></div>

      <h2>Six fresh seeds</h2>
      <div class="note">
        Sample six independent replicates at this width with the model's true reliability.
        Notice how often a genuinely imperfect width reports a flawless 6/6.
      </div>
      <div class="seedrow" id="seeds"></div>
      <button id="roll">Roll six seeds</button>
      <div class="readout" id="seedstat" style="margin-top:8px"></div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="panel" style="margin-top:18px">
    <h2 style="margin-top:0">The design rule, and the trade-off</h2>
    <div class="grid">
      <div>
        <table id="tbl"></table>
      </div>
      <div class="readout" id="design"></div>
    </div>
    <div class="note">
      The <span class="pill">necessary</span> width log<sub>p</sub>(1/ε) and the
      <span class="pill">sufficient</span> width log<sub>p</sub>(m/ε) differ only by the
      additive constant log<sub>p</sub> m: the knee is <em>located</em>, even though it is
      never <em>sharp</em>. Meanwhile the genericity of the private directions — the chance
      that k random draws really are independent, exactly
      <code>∏<sub>i<k</sub>(1 − p<sup>i−n</sup>)</code> — decays as k grows,
      so the best joint width is interior, near n/2.
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

<script>
const $ = id => document.getElementById(id);
const P = () => +$('p').value, M = () => +$('m').value, N = () => +$('n').value, K = () => +$('k').value;

function cure(p, k){ return 1 - Math.pow(p, -k); }
function envLow(p, k){ return Math.pow(p, -k); }
function envHigh(p, m, k){ return Math.min(1, m * Math.pow(p, -k)); }
function genericity(p, n, k){ let q = 1; for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) q *= (1 - Math.pow(p, i - n)); return q; }
function joint(p, n, m, k){ return 1 - m*Math.pow(p,-k) - (Math.pow(p,k)-1)/((p-1)*Math.pow(p,n)); }
function argmaxJoint(p, n, m){ let best = 0, bv = -Infinity;
  for (let k = 0; k <= n; k++){ const v = joint(p,n,m,k); if (v > bv){ bv = v; best = k; } } return best; }

const measured = [[0,0.25],[1,0.33],[2,0.83],[4,1.00],[8,1.00]];

function draw(){
  const c = $('plot'), g = c.getContext('2d');
  const W = c.width, H = c.height, L = 90, R = 30, T = 30, B = 70;
  const p = P(), m = M(), kmax = 16;
  g.clearRect(0,0,W,H);
  const X = k => L + (W-L-R) * k / kmax;
  const Y = v => T + (H-T-B) * (1 - v);

  // grid
  g.strokeStyle = 'rgba(255,255,255,.09)'; g.lineWidth = 1; g.font = '18px monospace';
  g.fillStyle = '#a3aad6';
  for (let i = 0; i <= 10; i++){
    const v = i/10, y = Y(v);
    g.beginPath(); g.moveTo(L,y); g.lineTo(W-R,y); g.stroke();
    g.textAlign = 'right'; g.fillText(v.toFixed(1), L-10, y+6);
  }
  for (let k = 0; k <= kmax; k += 2){
    const x = X(k);
    g.beginPath(); g.moveTo(x,T); g.lineTo(x,H-B); g.stroke();
    g.textAlign = 'center'; g.fillText(k, x, H-B+28);
  }
  g.textAlign='center'; g.fillStyle='#eef1ff'; g.font='20px sans-serif';
  g.fillText('exclusive dimensions  k', (L+W-R)/2, H-18);
  g.save(); g.translate(26,(T+H-B)/2); g.rotate(-Math.PI/2);
  g.fillText('reliability  P_cure(k)', 0, 0); g.restore();

  // envelope band: 1 - m p^-k  ..  1 - p^-k
  g.beginPath();
  for (let k = 0; k <= kmax; k++){ const x = X(k), y = Y(1 - envHigh(p,m,k)); k ? g.lineTo(x,y) : g.moveTo(x,y); }
  for (let k = kmax; k >= 0; k--){ g.lineTo(X(k), Y(1 - envLow(p,k))); }
  g.closePath(); g.fillStyle = 'rgba(90,209,255,.16)'; g.fill();

  // hypothetical cliff
  const kc = Math.max(1, Math.round(Math.log(m/0.05)/Math.log(p)));
  g.strokeStyle = '#ff6b8a'; g.setLineDash([9,7]); g.lineWidth = 2.5; g.beginPath();
  g.moveTo(X(0), Y(0)); g.lineTo(X(kc), Y(0)); g.lineTo(X(kc), Y(1)); g.lineTo(X(kmax), Y(1));
  g.stroke(); g.setLineDash([]);

  // exact curve
  g.strokeStyle = '#5ad1ff'; g.lineWidth = 3.5; g.beginPath();
  for (let k = 0; k <= kmax; k++){ const x = X(k), y = Y(cure(p,k)); k ? g.lineTo(x,y) : g.moveTo(x,y); }
  g.stroke();
  g.fillStyle = '#5ad1ff';
  for (let k = 0; k <= kmax; k++){ g.beginPath(); g.arc(X(k), Y(cure(p,k)), 5, 0, 7); g.fill(); }

  // measured stars
  g.fillStyle = '#ffd166';
  measured.forEach(([k,v]) => { star(g, X(k), Y(v), 11); });

  // certainty line
  g.strokeStyle = 'rgba(255,255,255,.45)'; g.setLineDash([4,6]); g.lineWidth = 1.5;
  g.beginPath(); g.moveTo(L, Y(1)); g.lineTo(W-R, Y(1)); g.stroke(); g.setLineDash([]);
  g.fillStyle = '#a3aad6'; g.textAlign='left'; g.font='17px sans-serif';
  g.fillText('certainty  (never attained)', L+12, Y(1)-10);

  // selected width marker
  const k0 = K();
  if (k0 <= kmax){
    g.strokeStyle = '#ffd166'; g.lineWidth = 2; g.setLineDash([3,5]);
    g.beginPath(); g.moveTo(X(k0), T); g.lineTo(X(k0), H-B); g.stroke(); g.setLineDash([]);
  }
}

function star(g,x,y,r){
  g.beginPath();
  for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++){
    const a = -Math.PI/2 + i*Math.PI/5, rr = i%2 ? r*0.45 : r;
    const px = x + rr*Math.cos(a), py = y + rr*Math.sin(a);
    i ? g.lineTo(px,py) : g.moveTo(px,py);
  }
  g.closePath(); g.fill();
}

function fmt(x, d=6){ return x.toLocaleString('en-US',{minimumFractionDigits:d,maximumFractionDigits:d}); }

function update(){
  $('pv').textContent = P(); $('mv').textContent = M();
  $('nv').textContent = N(); $('kv').textContent = K();
  const p = P(), m = M(), n = N(), k = Math.min(K(), n);
  const c = cure(p,k), gain = (p-1)/Math.pow(p,k+1);
  const gen = genericity(p,n,k), jb = joint(p,n,m,k), kopt = argmaxJoint(p,n,m);
  $('out').innerHTML =
    `exact reliability  <b>1 − p<sup>−k</sup> = ${fmt(c)}</b><br>`+
    `deficiency window  [${fmt(envLow(p,k),6)}, ${fmt(envHigh(p,m,k),6)}]<br>`+
    `next-dimension gain  <b>${fmt(gain)}</b><br>`+
    `genericity  ∏(1−p<sup>i−n</sup>) = ${fmt(gen,9)}<br>`+
    `joint bound f(k) = <b>${fmt(jb,9)}</b><br>`+
    `interior optimum  k* = <b>${kopt}</b> (n/2 = ${(n/2).toFixed(1)})`;

  let rows = '<tr><th>ε</th><th>necessary k</th><th>sufficient k</th><th>bracket</th></tr>';
  [0.5,0.25,0.1,0.05,0.01,0.001].forEach(e => {
    const nec = Math.ceil(Math.log(1/e)/Math.log(p));
    const suf = Math.max(nec, Math.ceil(Math.log(m/e)/Math.log(p)));
    rows += `<tr><td>${e}</td><td>${nec}</td><td>${suf}</td><td>${suf-nec}</td></tr>`;
  });
  $('tbl').innerHTML = rows;
  $('design').innerHTML =
    `<span class="pill">p = ${p}</span><span class="pill">m = ${m}</span><span class="pill">n = ${n}</span><br><br>`+
    `To reach reliability 1−ε you must spend at least<br>`+
    `<b>log<sub>${p}</sub>(1/ε)</b> exclusive dimensions, and<br>`+
    `<b>log<sub>${p}</sub>(${m}/ε)</b> always suffice.<br><br>`+
    `Bracket width = log<sub>${p}</sub> ${m} = <b>${(Math.log(m)/Math.log(p)).toFixed(2)}</b><br>`+
    `First dimension buys only <b>1 − 1/${p} = ${fmt(1-1/p,4)}</b>.`;
  draw();
}

function rollSeeds(){
  const p = P(), k = Math.min(K(), N()), tr = cure(p,k);
  let html = '', cures = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++){
    const ok = Math.random() < tr; if (ok) cures++;
    html += `<div class="seed ${ok?'cure':'fail'}">${ok?'✓':'✗'}</div>`;
  }
  $('seeds').innerHTML = html;
  const perfect = Math.pow(tr,6);
  $('seedstat').innerHTML =
    `observed <b>${cures}/6</b> cured  |  true reliability ${fmt(tr,4)}<br>`+
    `chance of a flawless 6/6 at this width: <b>${(100*perfect).toFixed(1)}%</b>`;
}

['p','m','n','k'].forEach(id => $(id).addEventListener('input', update));
$('roll').addEventListener('click', rollSeeds);
update(); rollSeeds();
</script>
</body>
</html>
"
    },
    {
      "title": "From Failure Masses to the Zeta Function: The Euler Bridge, and How a Cliff Would Break It",
      "description": "An interactive rendering of the number-theoretic identity behind the ramp. The exponent s and the truncation X are adjustable; the canvas plots the running product over characteristics p <= X of the width-damped failure masses sum_k p^{-ks} against the target zeta(s), computed live. A 'capacity cliff' switch truncates every local ramp at a user-chosen width K: the local series becomes a finite polynomial, the Euler factors shrink, and the running product visibly converges to the wrong value. This makes tangible the paper's sharpest structural claim -- the Euler-product identity holds precisely because the reliability ramp never terminates, so the existence of the bridge is itself an argument against a capacity cliff.",
      "html": "<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8"/>
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"/>
<title>From Failure Masses to the Zeta Function</title>
<style>
  :root{--bg:#0d1024;--panel:#171b38;--ink:#eef1ff;--muted:#a3aad6;--accent:#9be564;--accent2:#ffd166;--bad:#ff6b8a}
  *{box-sizing:border-box}
  body{margin:0;background:radial-gradient(1200px 700px at 20% -10%,#1b2350,#0b0e20 60%);
       color:var(--ink);font-family:-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,"Segoe UI",Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif}
  .wrap{max-width:1060px;margin:0 auto;padding:26px 18px 46px}
  h1{font-size:1.5rem;margin:0 0 6px}
  h2{font-size:1.02rem;color:var(--accent);margin:22px 0 8px}
  p.lede{color:var(--muted);line-height:1.6;margin:0 0 18px}
  .grid{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 330px;gap:18px}
  @media(max-width:900px){.grid{grid-template-columns:1fr}}
  .panel{background:rgba(23,27,56,.85);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.08);border-radius:14px;
         padding:16px 18px;box-shadow:0 10px 34px rgba(0,0,0,.4)}
  canvas{width:100%;height:auto;background:#0a0d20;border-radius:10px;display:block}
  label{display:block;font-size:.8rem;color:var(--muted);margin:14px 0 4px;letter-spacing:.09em;text-transform:uppercase}
  .val{float:right;color:var(--accent2);font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}
  input[type=range]{width:100%;accent-color:var(--accent)}

  .readout b{color:var(--accent)}
  .switch{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;margin-top:14px;font-size:.88rem;color:var(--muted)}
  .note{color:var(--muted);font-size:.86rem;line-height:1.6;margin-top:12px}

<body>
<div class="wrap">
  <h1>From Failure Masses to the Zeta Function</h1>
  <p class="lede">
    In the clean model the failure probability at exclusive width k is exactly
    p<sup>−k</sup>. Summing over all widths, with each width damped by an exponent s,
    gives the local factor Z<sub>p</sub>(s) = ∑<sub>k≥0</sub> p<sup>−ks</sup> =
    (1 − p<sup>−s</sup>)<sup>−1</sup>. Multiply these across every
    characteristic and you obtain the Riemann zeta function ζ(s). Flip the
    <em>cliff</em> switch to truncate every ramp at a finite width — the Euler factors
    collapse and the identity dies. The bridge exists <b>because</b> the ramp never ends.
  </p>

  <div class="grid">
    <div class="panel">
      <canvas id="cv" width="1280" height="640"></canvas>
      <div class="note">
        Green: the running product of the damped failure masses over characteristics
        p ≤ X. Gold dashed: the target ζ(s). With the cliff switch on, each local
        series is truncated at width K, the factors shrink, and the product stalls short of
        ζ(s) — a visual proof that a capacity cliff is incompatible with the
        Euler-product structure.
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="panel">
      <label>exponent s <span class="val" id="sv">2.0</span></label>
      <input id="s" type="range" min="1.1" max="6" step="0.1" value="2"/>
      <label>truncation X (characteristics up to) <span class="val" id="xv">200</span></label>
      <input id="x" type="range" min="5" max="2000" step="5" value="200"/>
      <div class="switch">
        <input type="checkbox" id="cliff"/><label for="cliff" style="margin:0;text-transform:none;letter-spacing:0">
        impose a capacity cliff: truncate each ramp at width K</label>
      </div>
      <label>cliff width K <span class="val" id="kv">3</span></label>
      <input id="k" type="range" min="1" max="12" step="1" value="3"/>

      <h2>Readout</h2>
      <div class="readout" id="out"></div>
      <div class="note">
        At s = 2 the target is π<sup>2</sup>/6 ≈ 1.644934. At s = 1 the product
        diverges: the total failure mass of the ramps, aggregated over all characteristics,
        is infinite — the arithmetic shadow of the fact that failure never disappears.
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

<script>
const $ = id => document.getElementById(id);
function primesUpTo(n){
  const sv = new Uint8Array(n+1).fill(1); sv[0]=sv[1]=0;
  for (let i=2;i*i<=n;i++) if (sv[i]) for (let j=i*i;j<=n;j+=i) sv[j]=0;
  const out=[]; for (let i=2;i<=n;i++) if (sv[i]) out.push(i); return out;
}
function localFactor(p, s, cliff, K){
  const r = Math.pow(p, -s);
  if (!cliff) return 1/(1-r);
  let sum = 0; for (let k=0;k<=K;k++) sum += Math.pow(r,k); return sum;   // truncated ramp
}
function zeta(s){ // Euler-Maclaurin-ish direct sum, plenty accurate for s > 1.1
  let sum = 0, N = 200000;
  for (let n=N;n>=1;n--) sum += Math.pow(n,-s);
  return sum + Math.pow(N,1-s)/(s-1) - Math.pow(N,-s)/2;
}
let zetaCache = {};
function zetaC(s){ const key=s.toFixed(2); if(!(key in zetaCache)) zetaCache[key]=zeta(s); return zetaCache[key]; }

function draw(){
  const s = +$('s').value, X = +$('x').value, cliff = $('cliff').checked, K = +$('k').value;
  $('sv').textContent = s.toFixed(1); $('xv').textContent = X; $('kv').textContent = K;

  const ps = primesUpTo(X), target = zetaC(s);
  const partial = []; let prod = 1;
  ps.forEach(p => { prod *= localFactor(p,s,cliff,K); partial.push(prod); });
  const finalVal = prod;

  const c=$('cv'), g=c.getContext('2d'), W=c.width,H=c.height,L=95,R=30,T=28,B=66;
  g.clearRect(0,0,W,H);
  const lo = 0.9, hi = Math.max(target*1.12, finalVal*1.06, 1.2);
  const Xp = i => L + (W-L-R)*(ps.length<2?1:i/(ps.length-1));
  const Yp = v => T + (H-T-B)*(1-(v-lo)/(hi-lo));

  g.strokeStyle='rgba(255,255,255,.09)'; g.font='17px monospace'; g.fillStyle='#a3aad6';
  for (let i=0;i<=8;i++){
    const v = lo + (hi-lo)*i/8, y = Yp(v);
    g.beginPath(); g.moveTo(L,y); g.lineTo(W-R,y); g.stroke();
    g.textAlign='right'; g.fillText(v.toFixed(3), L-10, y+6);
  }
  for (let i=0;i<=5;i++){
    const idx = Math.round((ps.length-1)*i/5), x = Xp(idx);
    g.beginPath(); g.moveTo(x,T); g.lineTo(x,H-B); g.stroke();
    g.textAlign='center'; g.fillText('p='+(ps[idx]||''), x, H-B+26);
  }
  g.fillStyle='#eef1ff'; g.font='19px sans-serif'; g.textAlign='center';
  g.fillText('characteristics included in the product', (L+W-R)/2, H-16);

  // target line
  g.strokeStyle='#ffd166'; g.setLineDash([8,7]); g.lineWidth=2.4;
  g.beginPath(); g.moveTo(L,Yp(target)); g.lineTo(W-R,Yp(target)); g.stroke(); g.setLineDash([]);
  g.fillStyle='#ffd166'; g.textAlign='left'; g.font='18px sans-serif';
  g.fillText('ζ(s) = '+target.toFixed(6), L+14, Yp(target)-12);

  // running product
  g.strokeStyle = cliff ? '#ff6b8a' : '#9be564'; g.lineWidth=3.4; g.beginPath();
  partial.forEach((v,i)=>{ const x=Xp(i), y=Yp(v); i?g.lineTo(x,y):g.moveTo(x,y); });
  g.stroke();
  g.fillStyle = cliff ? '#ff6b8a' : '#9be564';
  g.beginPath(); g.arc(Xp(partial.length-1), Yp(finalVal), 6, 0, 7); g.fill();

  const err = Math.abs(finalVal-target);
  $('out').innerHTML =

  "interactive_layout": "# How much private space does a full stop need?

Teaching a machine to *stop* sounds like the easiest job in the pipeline. It isn't. Train the same
sequence model five times with five random initialisations and you can get five different halting
behaviours: some copies stop flawlessly on inputs longer than anything they were trained on, some
trail off into gibberish, some stop *almost* always — and then don't, on the one long input you
cared about.

The folk explanation is that the boundary symbol needs **room**: coordinates in the representation
space that nothing else uses. Its own *exclusive dimensions*. And the folk corollary is that **one**
exclusive dimension ought to be enough — if there's a coordinate only the boundary symbol touches, a
linear readout can find it.

This page is about why that corollary is false, and about the exact shape of the truth. By the end
you will have derived, played with, and numerically verified a small theory: the reliability of a
boundary symbol as a function of its exclusive width is a **monotone ramp** — never decreasing, never
reaching certainty, climbing at exactly geometric rate — and, in a twist nobody ordered, its failure
spectrum is a local factor of the Riemann zeta function.

---

## 1. The measurement that started it

Fix a recurrent model completely: architecture, data, training schedule, everything. Let one number
vary — $E$, the number of coordinates the boundary token's learned representation may occupy, with
the rest zero-padded. Write $k$ for the resulting count of *exclusive* dimensions. Train six fresh
replicates at each width and ask one yes/no question of each: does it halt correctly, with
confidence $\ge 0.99$, on inputs longer than any it saw in training? Call such a replicate **cured**.

| exclusive dimensions $k$ | 0 | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fraction cured | $0.25$ | $0.33$ | $0.83$ | $1.00$ | $1.00$ |
| worst replicate | $0.005$ | $0.157$ | $0.948$ | $1.000$ | $1.000$ |

Read the $k=1$ row slowly. Two of six replicates were *perfect*; one scored $0.157$ — a hard failure.
Same width, same architecture, same data, different seed. Whatever exclusivity buys, it is not a
guarantee.

<details>
<summary><b>Why "cliff versus ramp" is the whole question</b></summary>

A **cliff** model says: below a critical width the mechanism is impossible, at or above it
guaranteed. A **ramp** model says: each extra exclusive dimension multiplies the failure rate by a
constant factor less than one, and no finite width eliminates failure.

They recommend different engineering (a hard budget versus a risk calculation), they predict
different sampling behaviour (deterministic versus binomial), and they license very different
conclusions from single-seed experiments. Six replicates per width cannot separate them — the
$k{=}1 \to k{=}2$ jump alone is not statistically significant. What *can* separate them is a model
that says what the alternatives look like. That's what we build next.
</details>

---

## 2. A model you can actually compute with

Reliability failures of this kind are **alignment** failures: the boundary token's private subspace
lines up with a degenerate direction of the trained dynamics, one along which the readout simply
cannot tell "stop" from "continue". Abstract away the mechanism and keep the geometry.

> **The model.** Let $V$ be a vector space of dimension $n$ over the finite field $\mathbb{F}_p$.
> The boundary token's exclusive subspace at width $k$ is generated by $k$ vectors
> $v_1,\dots,v_k$ drawn independently and uniformly from $V$ — one draw per exclusive dimension. The
> trained dynamics' degeneracies are a finite family of **proper** subspaces
> $W_1,\dots,W_m \subsetneq V$. A run **fails** when some $W_j$ swallows the *whole* exclusive
> subspace: $\exists j\ \forall i,\ v_i \in W_j$.

Everything is now finite, so "probability" means counting:
$$P_{\text{fail}}(k) = \frac{\#\{\text{failing } k\text{-tuples}\}}{|V|^{k}}, \qquad
P_{\text{cure}}(k) = 1 - P_{\text{fail}}(k).$$

Note how generous this is to the folk hypothesis: a *single* surviving direction outside every
obstruction already counts as success. And it still won't be enough.

---

## 3. Play with the ramp before you prove anything

The widget below *is* the theory. Drag $p$ (how coarse the field is), $m$ (how many degenerate modes
the system has), $n$ (the ambient width), and $k$ (the exclusive width you're buying). Three things
to try:

1. Push $k$ high and watch the blue curve approach — but never touch — the dotted certainty line.
2. Compare the blue ramp against the dashed red "capacity cliff". Nothing you can do to the sliders
   makes the ramp look like the cliff.
3. Hit **Roll six seeds** at $k = 4$, repeatedly. You will see 6/6 cured most of the time, at a width
   whose true reliability is only $0.94$. That is exactly how a ramp counterfeits a threshold.

{{interactive_demo:0}}

---

## 4. The four theorems, one at a time

### 4.1 Monotone: extra room never hurts

> **Theorem.** $P_{\text{cure}}(k)$ is nondecreasing in $k$.

<details>
<summary><b>Click to reveal the proof — it's one sentence and a bijection</b></summary>

Take any failing tuple of width $k+1$ and delete its last vector. What remains is a failing tuple of
width $k$: the obstruction that swallowed everything still contains the survivors. The map
$v \mapsto \big((v_1,\dots,v_k),\, v_{k+1}\big)$ is injective, so
$$N_{\text{fail}}(k+1) \le N_{\text{fail}}(k) \cdot |V|.$$
Divide by $|V|^{k+1}$: the failure *probability* cannot increase. $\blacksquare$

Notice how little the argument uses. No structure on the obstructions beyond being subspaces, no
properness, no independence. Monotonicity is essentially free.
</details>

### 4.2 Never certain: there is no capacity cliff

> **Theorem.** For every finite $k$, $P_{\text{fail}}(k) > 0$; hence $P_{\text{cure}}(k) < 1$ always,
> and the reliability curve is never a step function.

<details>
<summary><b>Click to reveal the proof — the witness is the zero vector</b></summary>

Every subspace contains $0$. So the draw $v_1 = \dots = v_k = 0$ fails at every width, forever.
There is always failing mass, hence never certainty. And a step function would require
$P_{\text{cure}}(k_0) = 1$ at its jump, which cannot happen. $\blacksquare$

Consequence for the data: the measured $100\%$ at $k = 4$ and $k = 8$ *must* be a finite-sample
effect under the model. Enough replicates would eventually turn up a failure.
</details>

### 4.3 Geometric: the ramp is pinned between two exponentials

> **Theorem.** If all obstructions are proper and at least one is a hyperplane (index exactly $p$),
> then for every $k$
> $$\frac{1}{p^{k}} \;\le\; 1 - P_{\text{cure}}(k) \;\le\; \frac{m}{p^{k}}.$$

<details>
<summary><b>Click to reveal both bounds</b></summary>

*Upper (union bound).* A proper subspace has index at least $p$, so it contains at most $|V|/p$
vectors; the chance that all $k$ independent draws land inside one fixed obstruction is at most
$p^{-k}$. Sum over the $m$ obstructions.

*Lower.* If $W_j$ has index exactly $p$ then the tuples inside it number exactly $(|V|/p)^k$, and
every one of them fails. So $P_{\text{fail}}(k) \ge p^{-k}$. $\blacksquare$

Both bounds have the *same* geometric ratio $1/p$ and differ only by the constant $m$. That rules
out a super-geometric collapse (a cliff) and a sub-geometric decay (a plateau) simultaneously.
</details>

### 4.4 Exact, and sublinear

With a single hyperplane obstruction the curve is exact:
$$P_{\text{cure}}(k) = 1 - p^{-k}.$$
Two immediate corollaries. First, $P_{\text{cure}}(0) = 0$: no exclusive room, no reliability.
Second — the punchline —
$$P_{\text{cure}}(1) = 1 - \frac{1}{p} \;<\; 1: \qquad \textbf{the first exclusive dimension is not sufficient.}$$
And the marginal value of the $(k+1)$-st dimension is exactly $(p-1)/p^{k+1}$, strictly decreasing:
diminishing returns, quantified. At $p = 2$ the curve reads $0,\ \tfrac12,\ \tfrac34,\ \tfrac{15}{16},
\ \tfrac{255}{256}$ at the tested widths $0,1,2,4,8$ — the same shape, the same knee, and the honest
prediction that the two measured $1.00$s are really $0.94$ and $0.996$ sampled six times each.

{{visualization:0}}

## 5. The design rule: a located knee without a sharp one

Rearranging the two bounds of §4.3 gives a matched pair.

- **Necessary:** reliability $1-\epsilon$ forces $k \ge \log_p(1/\epsilon)$.
- **Sufficient:** $k \ge \log_p(m/\epsilon)$ guarantees reliability $1-\epsilon$.

They differ by the *additive* constant $\log_p m$ — never by a multiplicative factor. So the knee's
**location** is pinned even though the knee has no **sharpness** at all. Calibrated at $p = 2$ with
$m$ around $8$–$16$ degenerate modes, this reproduces the empirical prescription:

> **Reserve at least four exclusive dimensions for a boundary token.** Two is near-robust; one is a
> coin flip dressed up as a design.

## 6. Are the "exclusive" dimensions actually exclusive?

A subtlety the phrase hides: we drew $k$ random vectors and called their span $k$-dimensional. Random
vectors can be dependent. Does the model quietly overclaim?

> **Theorem ($q$-Pochhammer genericity).** The probability that $k$ uniform draws from an
> $n$-dimensional space over $\mathbb{F}_p$ are linearly independent is exactly
> $$\prod_{i=0}^{k-1}\left(1 - \frac{p^{i}}{p^{n}}\right) \;\ge\; 1 - \frac{p^{k}-1}{(p-1)p^{n}}.$$

<details>
<summary><b>Click to reveal the counting argument and the inequality</b></summary>

Having chosen $i$ independent vectors, the $(i+1)$-st must avoid their span, a subspace of exactly
$p^{i}$ elements. So the number of independent $k$-tuples is $\prod_{i<k}(p^{n} - p^{i})$; divide by
$|V|^{k} = p^{nk}$ to get the product. This is a truncated
[$q$-Pochhammer symbol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Q-Pochhammer_symbol), the same object that
counts [subspaces and flags over finite fields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaussian_binomial_coefficient).

For the bound, use the elementary **Weierstrass product inequality** $1 - \sum a_i \le \prod(1-a_i)$
for $a_i \in [0,1]$ — an easy induction: with $S = \sum_{i<k} a_i$,
$$\prod_{i \le k}(1-a_i) \ge (1-S)(1-a_k) = 1 - S - a_k + Sa_k \ge 1 - S - a_k.$$
Then sum the geometric series $\sum_{i<k} p^{i} = (p^{k}-1)/(p-1)$. $\blacksquare$
</details>

At the experimental scale — $p = 2$, ambient width $n = 192$, $k \le 8$ — the genericity loss is
about $2^{-184}$. The exclusive dimensions are exclusive; the model isn't vacuous.

But notice the *direction*. Reliability error shrinks like $p^{-k}$; genericity error **grows** like
$p^{k-n}$. Combining them, the probability that the boundary token both occupies a genuinely
$k$-dimensional subspace *and* escapes every obstruction is at least
$$f(k) = 1 - \frac{m}{p^{k}} - \frac{p^{k}-1}{(p-1)p^{n}}.$$
Two opposed geometric forces, hence a smooth **interior** optimum near $k \approx n/2$ — and this is
the deepest structural reason the reliability curve cannot be a cliff. A cliff is what a single
monotone force produces. Here two forces act.

## 7. The guest nobody invited: $\zeta(s)$

One last turn. In the clean model the failure probability at width $k$ is exactly $p^{-k}$. What is
the **total failure mass** of the ramp, summed over all widths?
$$\sum_{k \ge 0} p^{-k} = \frac{p}{p-1} = \left(1 - \frac{1}{p}\right)^{-1}.$$

That is the local [Euler factor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler_product) of the Riemann zeta
function at $p$. Damp each width by an exponent $s$ — weight a width-$k$ failure by $p^{-ks}$ — and
the local mass becomes $(1-p^{-s})^{-1}$ exactly. Now recall that the characteristic $p$ was a free
parameter: every prime gives a different ramp. Multiply them all:
$$\prod_{p \text{ prime}} \sum_{k \ge 0} p^{-ks} \;=\; \zeta(s), \qquad \operatorname{Re} s > 1,$$
so at $s = 2$ the product of the damped failure masses across all characteristics is $\pi^2/6$.

The moral is sharper than the identity. **An Euler factor exists because the local series is
infinite.** A capacity cliff would truncate every local sum to a polynomial and the product would
converge to the wrong thing. Toggle the cliff switch below and watch the identity break in real
time.

## 9. What to take away

* **Monotone ramp.** Reliability never decreases with exclusive width, never reaches $1$, and
  converges to $1$: no capacity cliff exists.
* **Geometric envelope.** $p^{-k} \le 1 - P_{\text{cure}}(k) \le m\,p^{-k}$ — the deficiency decays at
  exactly geometric rate, so the knee is located to within $\log_p m$ while never being sharp.
* **One dimension is not enough.** $P_{\text{cure}}(1) = 1 - 1/p$, and the marginal value of each
  further dimension, $(p-1)p^{-(k+1)}$, strictly decreases.
* **Genericity costs.** Independence of the drawn directions holds with probability
  $\prod_{i<k}(1-p^{i-n})$, decreasing in $k$; the joint optimum is interior.
* **Euler bridge.** The ramp's damped failure masses multiply over all characteristics to $\zeta(s)$,
  and this can only happen because the ramp is infinite.

And a methodological coda that outlives the example. At any width where the true failure rate is
$0.2$, five out of six replicates look like a clean success, and a single-replicate study looks like
a discovered threshold. **Ramps masquerade as cliffs routinely.** The cure is not more precision at
one width; it is measurement across several widths, read against a model that tells you what the
alternatives could possibly look like.

# Are the exclusive dimensions really exclusive?  A `q`-Pochhammer genericity bound

Companion to `Catalog/NumberTheory/EOSWidthMonotoneRamp.lean`.

The ramp model draws the boundary token's `k` exclusive directions uniformly at random from a
finite `𝔽_p`-space `V` of dimension `n`.  For the phrase "`k` exclusive dimensions" to be
honest, the `k` draws must actually be linearly independent.  This file quantifies that:

* `EOSGenericity.probIndep_eq_prod` — the probability that `k ≤ n` uniform draws are linearly
  independent is exactly the `q`-Pochhammer product `∏_{i<k} (1 - p^{i-n})`
  (via Mathlib's `card_linearIndependent`);
* `EOSGenericity.one_sub_sum_le_prod_one_sub` — a Weierstrass product inequality, proved by
  induction;
* `EOSGenericity.probIndep_ge` — hence `P(independent) ≥ 1 - (p^k - 1)/((p-1) p^n)`: for
  `k ≪ n` the drawn directions are exclusive with overwhelming probability, so the model of
  the companion file is not vacuous;
* `EOSGenericity.probIndep_antitone_step` — genericity decays with `k`, in the opposite
  direction to the reliability ramp;
* `EOSGenericity.prob_indep_and_cure_ge` — **the synthesis**: with `k` exclusive dimensions the
  probability that the token both occupies a genuine `k`-dimensional subspace *and* escapes all
  `m` obstructions is at least

  `1 - m·p^{-k} - (p^k - 1)/((p-1)·p^n)`,

  a two-sided window: the first term (reliability) shrinks geometrically in `k`, the second
  (genericity) grows geometrically in `k`, so the optimal exclusive width is interior — there is
  a genuine trade-off and no cliff.

### Lab notes

With `p = 2`, `n = 192` (the hidden width of the recurrent cell in the motivating experiment)
and `m = 1`, the bound reads `1 - 2^{-k} - (2^k-1)·2^{-192}`: the genericity loss is utterly
negligible up to `k ≈ 100`, so in the regime of the data (`k ≤ 8`) the reliability term alone
governs, matching the observed monotone ramp `0.25 → 0.33 → 0.83 → 1.00 → 1.00`.
-/

import Mathlib
import NumberTheory.EOSWidthMonotoneRamp

open Module Finset

namespace EOSGenericity

variable {p m : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module (ZMod p) V] [Finite V]

/-- Probability that `k` uniform draws from `V` are linearly independent. -/
noncomputable def probIndep (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (V : Type*) [AddCommGroup V]
    [Module (ZMod p) V] [Finite V] (k : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  (Nat.card {s : Fin k → V // LinearIndependent (ZMod p) s} : ℝ) / (Nat.card V : ℝ) ^ k

/-- **`q`-Pochhammer formula.**  For `k ≤ dim V` the genericity probability is exactly
`∏_{i<k} (1 - p^{i}/p^{n})`. -/
theorem probIndep_eq_prod {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ finrank (ZMod p) V) :
    probIndep p V k
      = ∏ i ∈ range k, (1 - (p : ℝ) ^ i / (p : ℝ) ^ (finrank (ZMod p) V)) := by
  classical
  have hp : 1 < p := (Fact.out : p.Prime).one_lt
  have hpR : (1 : ℝ) < (p : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hp
  set n := finrank (ZMod p) V with hn
  have hcardV : Nat.card V = p ^ n := EOSWidthRamp.card_eq_pow_finrank_zmod (p := p) V
  have hq : Fintype.card (ZMod p) = p := ZMod.card p
  have hcount : Nat.card {s : Fin k → V // LinearIndependent (ZMod p) s}
      = ∏ i : Fin k, (p ^ n - p ^ (i : ℕ)) := by
    have := card_linearIndependent (K := ZMod p) (V := V) (k := k) (by simpa [hn] using hk)
    simpa [hq, hn] using this
  have hcast : ((∏ i : Fin k, (p ^ n - p ^ (i : ℕ)) : ℕ) : ℝ)
      = ∏ i ∈ range k, ((p : ℝ) ^ n - (p : ℝ) ^ i) := by
    rw [Nat.cast_prod, Fin.prod_univ_eq_prod_range (fun i => ((p ^ n - p ^ i : ℕ) : ℝ))]
    refine Finset.prod_congr rfl fun i hi => ?_
    have hle : p ^ i ≤ p ^ n :=
      Nat.pow_le_pow_right (le_of_lt hp) (le_trans (le_of_lt (mem_range.mp hi)) hk)
    push_cast [Nat.cast_sub hle]
    ring
  have hpow : (0 : ℝ) < (p : ℝ) ^ n := by positivity
  rw [probIndep, hcount, hcast, hcardV]
  push_cast
  rw [← pow_mul]
  have : ∏ i ∈ range k, ((p : ℝ) ^ n - (p : ℝ) ^ i)
      = (∏ i ∈ range k, (1 - (p : ℝ) ^ i / (p : ℝ) ^ n)) * ((p : ℝ) ^ n) ^ k := by
    have hfac : ∀ i ∈ range k, ((p : ℝ) ^ n - (p : ℝ) ^ i)
        = (1 - (p : ℝ) ^ i / (p : ℝ) ^ n) * (p : ℝ) ^ n := by
      intro i _
      field_simp
    rw [Finset.prod_congr rfl hfac, Finset.prod_mul_distrib, Finset.prod_const, card_range]
  rw [this, pow_mul]
  field_simp

/-- **Weierstrass product inequality** (proved by induction): for `0 ≤ aᵢ ≤ 1`,
`1 - ∑ aᵢ ≤ ∏ (1 - aᵢ)`. -/
theorem one_sub_sum_le_prod_one_sub (a : ℕ → ℝ) (k : ℕ)
    (h0 : ∀ i ∈ range k, 0 ≤ a i) (h1 : ∀ i ∈ range k, a i ≤ 1) :
    1 - ∑ i ∈ range k, a i ≤ ∏ i ∈ range k, (1 - a i) := by
  induction k with
  | zero => simp
  | succ k ih =>
      have h0' : ∀ i ∈ range k, 0 ≤ a i := fun i hi =>
        h0 i (mem_range.mpr (lt_trans (mem_range.mp hi) (Nat.lt_succ_self k)))
      have h1' : ∀ i ∈ range k, a i ≤ 1 := fun i hi =>
        h1 i (mem_range.mpr (lt_trans (mem_range.mp hi) (Nat.lt_succ_self k)))
      have hstep := ih h0' h1'
      have hak0 : 0 ≤ a k := h0 k (mem_range.mpr (Nat.lt_succ_self k))
      have hak1 : a k ≤ 1 := h1 k (mem_range.mpr (Nat.lt_succ_self k))
      have hsum0 : 0 ≤ ∑ i ∈ range k, a i := Finset.sum_nonneg h0'
      rw [Finset.prod_range_succ, Finset.sum_range_succ]
      have hmul : (1 - ∑ i ∈ range k, a i) * (1 - a k)
          ≤ (∏ i ∈ range k, (1 - a i)) * (1 - a k) :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hstep (by linarith)
      nlinarith [hmul, hsum0, hak0]

/-- **Genericity bound.**  `k` uniform draws are linearly independent with probability at least
`1 - (p^k - 1)/((p-1) p^n)`. -/
theorem probIndep_ge {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ finrank (ZMod p) V) :
    1 - ((p : ℝ) ^ k - 1) / (((p : ℝ) - 1) * (p : ℝ) ^ (finrank (ZMod p) V))
      ≤ probIndep p V k := by
  have hp : 1 < p := (Fact.out : p.Prime).one_lt
  have hpR : (1 : ℝ) < (p : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hp
  set n := finrank (ZMod p) V with hn
  have hpow : (0 : ℝ) < (p : ℝ) ^ n := by positivity
  have hsum : ∑ i ∈ range k, (p : ℝ) ^ i / (p : ℝ) ^ n
      = ((p : ℝ) ^ k - 1) / (((p : ℝ) - 1) * (p : ℝ) ^ n) := by
    rw [← Finset.sum_div, geom_sum_eq (by linarith)]
    field_simp
  rw [probIndep_eq_prod hk, ← hsum]
  refine one_sub_sum_le_prod_one_sub _ k (fun i _ => by positivity) (fun i hi => ?_)
  have hle : (p : ℝ) ^ i ≤ (p : ℝ) ^ n :=
    pow_le_pow_right₀ (le_of_lt hpR) (le_trans (le_of_lt (mem_range.mp hi)) hk)
  rw [div_le_one hpow]
  exact hle

/-- Genericity decays with the width: one more draw can only make independence harder. -/
theorem probIndep_antitone_step {k : ℕ} (hk : k + 1 ≤ finrank (ZMod p) V) :
    probIndep p V (k + 1) ≤ probIndep p V k := by
  have hp : 1 < p := (Fact.out : p.Prime).one_lt
  have hpR : (1 : ℝ) < (p : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hp
  set n := finrank (ZMod p) V with hn
  have hk' : k ≤ n := by omega
  rw [probIndep_eq_prod hk, probIndep_eq_prod hk', Finset.prod_range_succ]
  have hnn : ∀ i ∈ range k, (0 : ℝ) ≤ 1 - (p : ℝ) ^ i / (p : ℝ) ^ n := by
    intro i hi
    have hle : (p : ℝ) ^ i ≤ (p : ℝ) ^ n :=
      pow_le_pow_right₀ (le_of_lt hpR) (le_trans (le_of_lt (mem_range.mp hi)) hk')
    have : (p : ℝ) ^ i / (p : ℝ) ^ n ≤ 1 := by
      rw [div_le_one (by positivity)]; exact hle
    linarith
  have hprod : (0 : ℝ) ≤ ∏ i ∈ range k, (1 - (p : ℝ) ^ i / (p : ℝ) ^ n) :=
    Finset.prod_nonneg hnn
  have hfac : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (p : ℝ) ^ k / (p : ℝ) ^ n := by positivity
  nlinarith [hprod, hfac]

theorem prob_indep_and_cure_ge (W : Fin m → Submodule (ZMod p) V) (hW : ∀ j, W j ≠ ⊤) {k : ℕ}

## Motivation (NET-27, `EOS-WIDTH-SHIFT-IS-A-MONOTONE-RAMP`)

| exclusive dims `k` | 0    | 1    | 2    | 4    | 8    |
|--------------------|------|------|------|------|------|
| `P(cure)`          | 0.25 | 0.33 | 0.83 | 1.00 | 1.00 |

*sublinear* (diminishing returns), and there is *no sharp critical width* — one exclusive
dimension is not sufficient, but no finite width makes success certain either.

not observations.  Let `V` be a finite vector space over `𝔽_p` (`p` prime).  The boundary
token's exclusive subspace is modelled by a tuple `v : Fin k → V` of `k` independent
uniform draws, and the network's failure modes by a finite family `W : Fin m → Submodule 𝔽_p V`
of *proper* subspaces ("obstruction subspaces"): the run *fails* when the whole exclusive
subspace is swallowed by some obstruction, i.e. when `∃ j, ∀ i, v i ∈ W j`.

* `EOSWidthRamp.failProb_antitone` / `EOSWidthRamp.cureProb_monotone` — **monotone ramp**;
* `EOSWidthRamp.failProb_pos` — failure probability is *strictly positive for every `k`*:

* `EOSWidthRamp.failProb_le` — union bound `P(fail) ≤ m · p^{-k}`: the curve does climb to 1;

/-- A finite `𝔽_p`-vector space has `p ^ dim` elements. -/
theorem card_eq_pow_finrank_zmod (W : Type*) [AddCommGroup W] [Module (ZMod p) W] [Finite W] :
    Nat.card W = p ^ finrank (ZMod p) W := by
  have := Fintype.ofFinite W

theorem card_submodule_mul_le {W : Submodule (ZMod p) V} (hW : W ≠ ⊤) :

  have hp : 1 < p := (Fact.out : p.Prime).one_lt
  have hlt : finrank (ZMod p) W < finrank (ZMod p) V := Submodule.finrank_lt hW
  calc Nat.card W * p = p ^ (finrank (ZMod p) W + 1) := by

width `k`. -/
noncomputable def failCount (W : Fin m → Submodule (ZMod p) V) (k : ℕ) : ℕ :=

noncomputable def failProb (W : Fin m → Submodule (ZMod p) V) (k : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  (failCount W k : ℝ) / (Nat.card V : ℝ) ^ k

/-- The reliability ("cure") probability at exclusive width `k`. -/
noncomputable def cureProb (W : Fin m → Submodule (ZMod p) V) (k : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  1 - failProb W k

/-- The `k`-tuples inside a fixed subspace `W` number `(#W)^k`. -/
theorem card_tuples_mem (W : Submodule (ZMod p) V) (k : ℕ) :
    Nat.card {v : Fin k → V // ∀ i, v i ∈ W} = (Nat.card W) ^ k := by
  have e : {v : Fin k → V // ∀ i, v i ∈ W} ≃ (Fin k → W) :=

/-! ## The abstract notion of a monotone ramp -/

/-- A *monotone ramp*: a reliability curve that never decreases, never attains certainty,
and converges to certainty.  Such a curve has no critical width. -/
structure IsMonotoneRamp (P : ℕ → ℝ) : Prop where
  mono : Monotone P
  lt_one : ∀ k, P k < 1
  tendsto_one : Tendsto P atTop (𝓝 1)

/-- **No capacity cliff.**  A monotone ramp never attains certainty, so there is no width
beyond which success is guaranteed. -/
theorem IsMonotoneRamp.no_critical_width {P : ℕ → ℝ} (h : IsMonotoneRamp P) :
    ¬ ∃ k, ∀ l, k ≤ l → P l = 1 := by
  rintro ⟨k, hk⟩
  exact absurd (hk k le_rfl) (ne_of_lt (h.lt_one k))

/-- Yet the ramp gets arbitrarily close to certainty. -/
theorem IsMonotoneRamp.eventually_gt {P : ℕ → ℝ} (h : IsMonotoneRamp P) {c : ℝ} (hc : c < 1) :
    ∃ K, ∀ l, K ≤ l → c < P l := by
  have := h.tendsto_one.eventually (eventually_gt_nhds hc)
  obtain ⟨K, hK⟩ := this.exists_forall_of_atTop
  exact ⟨K, fun l hl => hK l hl⟩

reliability curve `k ↦ P(cure)` is a monotone ramp: nondecreasing, strictly below `1` at
every finite width, and converging to `1`. -/
theorem cureProb_isMonotoneRamp (W : Fin m → Submodule (ZMod p) V) (hm : 0 < m)
    (hW : ∀ j, W j ≠ ⊤) : IsMonotoneRamp (cureProb W) := by
  refine ⟨cureProb_monotone W, cureProb_lt_one W hm, ?_⟩
  have hp : 1 < p := (Fact.out : p.Prime).one_lt
  have hlow : Tendsto (fun k : ℕ => 1 - (m : ℝ) / (p : ℝ) ^ k) atTop (𝓝 1) := by
    have h0 : Tendsto (fun k : ℕ => ((p : ℝ)⁻¹) ^ k) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
      apply tendsto_pow_atTop_nhds_zero_of_lt_one (by positivity)
      rw [inv_lt_one_iff₀]
      right
      exact_mod_cast hp
    have : Tendsto (fun k : ℕ => (m : ℝ) * ((p : ℝ)⁻¹) ^ k) atTop (𝓝 ((m : ℝ) * 0)) :=
      h0.const_mul _
    have h2 : Tendsto (fun k : ℕ => 1 - (m : ℝ) * ((p : ℝ)⁻¹) ^ k) atTop (𝓝 (1 - (m : ℝ) * 0)) :=

from __future__ import annotations

import itertools
import math
import random
from fractions import Fraction
from typing import Callable, Iterable, Iterator, List, Sequence, Tuple

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Brute-force ground truth over small finite vector spaces
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def all_vectors(p: int, n: int) -> Iterator[Tuple[int, ...]]:
    """Enumerate every vector of F_p^n as a tuple of residues."""
    return itertools.product(range(p), repeat=n)


def in_kernel(v: Sequence[int], functionals: Sequence[Sequence[int]], p: int) -> bool:
    """True iff v lies in the common kernel of the given linear functionals over F_p."""
    for a in functionals:
        if sum(ai * vi for ai, vi in zip(a, v)) % p != 0:
            return False
    return True


def brute_force_fail_prob(
    p: int, n: int, obstructions: Sequence[Sequence[Sequence[int]]], k: int
) -> Fraction:
    """
    Exact P_fail(k) by full enumeration of V^k.

    Each obstruction is given as a list of linear functionals (rows); the obstruction
    subspace is their common kernel.  A tuple fails iff some obstruction contains all
    of its k entries.
    """
    vectors: List[Tuple[int, ...]] = list(all_vectors(p, n))
    # Precompute, for each obstruction, the set of vectors it contains.
    members: List[set] = [
        {v for v in vectors if in_kernel(v, obs, p)} for obs in obstructions
    ]
    total = 0
    failing = 0
    for tup in itertools.product(vectors, repeat=k):
        total += 1
        if any(all(v in mem for v in tup) for mem in members):
            failing += 1
    return Fraction(failing, total)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Closed-form curves
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def hyperplane_cure_prob(p: int, k: int) -> Fraction:
    """Exact reliability of the single-hyperplane model: 1 - p^{-k}."""
    return Fraction(1) - Fraction(1, p**k)


def marginal_gain(p: int, k: int) -> Fraction:
    """Reliability bought by the (k+1)-st exclusive dimension: (p-1)/p^{k+1}."""
    return Fraction(p - 1, p ** (k + 1))


def envelope(p: int, m: int, k: int) -> Tuple[Fraction, Fraction]:
    """Two-sided envelope (lower, upper) for the deficiency 1 - P_cure(k)."""
    return Fraction(1, p**k), Fraction(m, p**k)


def inclusion_exclusion_fail_prob(p: int, k: int, codims: dict) -> Fraction:
    """
    Exact P_fail(k) by inclusion-exclusion, given a dict mapping each nonempty subset
    S (as a frozenset of obstruction indices) to codim of the intersection of the W_j,
    j in S.
    """
    total = Fraction(0)
    for subset, codim in codims.items():
        sign = 1 if len(subset) % 2 == 1 else -1
        total += sign * Fraction(1, p ** (k * codim))
    return total


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Design rule
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def required_widths(p: int, m: int, eps: float) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    """
    Return (necessary, sufficient) exclusive widths for reliability 1 - eps:
    necessary  k >= log_p(1/eps),  sufficient k >= log_p(m/eps).
    """
    necessary = math.ceil(math.log(1.0 / eps, p))
    sufficient = math.ceil(math.log(m / eps, p))
    return necessary, sufficient

# 4. Genericity: the q-Pochhammer product
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def prob_independent_exact(p: int, n: int, k: int) -> Fraction:
    """Exact P_ind(k) = prod_{i<k} (1 - p^{i-n}) for k <= n."""
    assert k <= n, "need k <= n"
    prod = Fraction(1)
    for i in range(k):
        prod *= Fraction(1) - Fraction(p**i, p**n)
    return prod


def prob_independent_lower_bound(p: int, n: int, k: int) -> Fraction:
    """Closed-form Weierstrass bound 1 - (p^k - 1)/((p-1) p^n)."""
    return Fraction(1) - Fraction(p**k - 1, (p - 1) * p**n)


def joint_lower_bound(p: int, n: int, m: int, k: int) -> Fraction:
    """1 - m p^{-k} - (p^k - 1)/((p-1) p^n): reliability AND genericity."""
    return (
        Fraction(1)
        - Fraction(m, p**k)
        - Fraction(p**k - 1, (p - 1) * p**n)
    )


def argmax_joint(p: int, n: int, m: int) -> int:
    """Exclusive width maximising the joint lower bound (exhaustive over 0..n)."""
    return max(range(n + 1), key=lambda k: joint_lower_bound(p, n, m, k))


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Euler bridge
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def primes_up_to(limit: int) -> List[int]:
    """Sieve of Eratosthenes."""
    sieve = [True] * (limit + 1)
    sieve[0:2] = [False, False]
    for i in range(2, int(limit**0.5) + 1):
        if sieve[i]:
            for j in range(i * i, limit + 1, i):
                sieve[j] = False
    return [i for i, ok in enumerate(sieve) if ok]


def ramp_series(p: int, s: float, terms: int = 400) -> float:
    """Width-damped failure mass sum_{k>=0} p^{-ks} of the ramp at characteristic p."""
    return sum((p ** (-s)) ** k for k in range(terms))


def euler_product(s: float, limit: int) -> float:
    """Product over primes p <= limit of the damped failure masses."""
    prod = 1.0
    for p in primes_up_to(limit):
        prod *= ramp_series(p, s)
    return prod


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Monte-Carlo cross-check
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def monte_carlo_fail_rate(
    p: int, n: int, k: int, trials: int, seed: int = 0
) -> float:
    """
    Estimate P_fail(k) for the single hyperplane {x : x_0 + x_1 + ... + x_{n-1} = 0}
    by uniform sampling of k-tuples from F_p^n.  Should converge to p^{-k}.
    """
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    fails = 0
    for _ in range(trials):
        ok = True
        for _ in range(k):
            v = [rng.randrange(p) for _ in range(n)]
            if sum(v) % p != 0:
                ok = False
                break
        if ok:
            fails += 1
    return fails / trials


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Driver
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def rule(title: str) -> None:
    print()
    print("=" * 78)
    print(title)
    print("=" * 78)


def main() -> None:

        meas = f"{MEASURED[k]:.2f}" if k in MEASURED else "-"
        print(
            f"{k:>3} {str(model):>14} = {float(model):>8.6f} {meas:>10} "
            f"{str(marginal_gain(2, k)):>14}"
        )

    print("Marginal gains (p-1)/p^{k+1} strictly decrease: sublinear benefit.")
    print("P_cure(k) < 1 for every finite k: no capacity cliff, ever.")

    rule("2. Brute-force verification of the model over F_2^3 and F_3^2")
    # Single hyperplane in F_2^3: kernel of the functional (1,1,1).

        (3, 2, [[(1, 2)]], "F_3^2, one hyperplane"),
        (2, 3, [[(1, 1, 1)], [(1, 0, 0)]], "F_2^3, two hyperplanes"),
    ]:

        print(f"{'k':>3} {'P_fail (exact count)':>22} {'lower p^-k':>12} {'upper m p^-k':>14}")
        for k in range(0, 4):

            flag = "ok" if lo <= pf <= hi else "VIOLATION"
            print(f"{k:>3} {str(pf):>22} {str(lo):>12} {str(hi):>14}  {flag}")
        # monotonicity
        vals = [brute_force_fail_prob(p, n, obs, k) for k in range(4)]
        print("  P_fail antitone:", all(vals[i + 1] <= vals[i] for i in range(3)))
        print("  P_fail > 0 at every width:", all(v > 0 for v in vals))

    print(f"{'p':>3} {'m':>4} {'eps':>8} {'necessary k':>12} {'sufficient k':>13} {'gap':>5}")

    print("width lands at 8, the necessary at 5; the empirical prescription 'reserve")
    print(">= 4 exclusive dimensions' sits exactly in this bracket.")

    rule("5. q-Pochhammer genericity: the exclusive dimensions really are exclusive")
    print(f"{'p':>3} {'n':>5} {'k':>3} {'P_ind (exact)':>20} {'lower bound':>20} {'1 - P_ind':>14}")
    for p, n, k in [(2, 8, 4), (2, 16, 8), (2, 64, 8), (2, 192, 8), (3, 20, 5)]:
        exact = prob_independent_exact(p, n, k)
        lower = prob_independent_lower_bound(p, n, k)
        assert lower <= exact, "Weierstrass bound violated"
        print(
            f"{p:>3} {n:>5} {k:>3} {float(exact):>20.15f} {float(lower):>20.15f} "
            f"{float(1 - exact):>14.3e}"
        )
    print("\nAt the experimental scale (p = 2, ambient width n = 192, k <= 8) the")
    print("genericity loss is about 2^-184: the model is not vacuous.")
    print("\nGenericity is antitone in k (p = 2, n = 12):")
    prev = None
    for k in range(0, 7):
        val = prob_independent_exact(2, 12, k)
        mark = "" if prev is None else ("  <= previous" if val <= prev else "  INCREASE!")
        print(f"  k = {k}: P_ind = {float(val):.12f}{mark}")
        prev = val

    rule("6. Reliability vs genericity: the optimum is INTERIOR")
    for p, n, m in [(2, 16, 1), (2, 16, 8), (2, 32, 8), (3, 18, 4)]:
        best = argmax_joint(p, n, m)
        predicted = 0.5 * (n + math.log(m * (p - 1), p)) if m * (p - 1) > 0 else n / 2

            f"\np = {p}, n = {n}, m = {m}:  argmax_k f(k) = {best}   "

        print(f"{'k':>4} {'f(k) = 1 - m p^-k - (p^k-1)/((p-1)p^n)':>42}")
        for k in range(max(0, best - 3), min(n, best + 4)):

    print("\nThe reliability error decays like p^-k; the genericity error grows like")
    print("p^{k-n}.  Two opposed geometric forces => a smooth interior maximum, which")
    print("is the structural reason the reliability curve cannot be a cliff.")

    rule("7. Monte-Carlo cross-check of the exact curve P_fail(k) = p^-k")
    print(f"{'k':>3} {'sampled rate':>14} {'exact p^-k':>12} {'trials':>9}")
    for k in range(0, 5):
        est = monte_carlo_fail_rate(2, 6, k, trials=200_000, seed=12345 + k)
        print(f"{k:>3} {est:>14.5f} {2.0 ** (-k):>12.5f} {200000:>9}")

    rule("8. The Euler bridge: ramp failure masses multiply to zeta(s)")
    print("Total failure mass at characteristic p (s = 1):  sum_k p^-k = p/(p-1)")
    for p in [2, 3, 5, 7, 11]:
        print(f"  p = {p:>2}:  {ramp_series(p, 1.0):.10f}   vs  p/(p-1) = {p / (p - 1):.10f}")
    print("\nProduct over primes p <= X of the damped masses, versus zeta(s):")
    for s, target, name in [
        (2.0, math.pi**2 / 6, "zeta(2) = pi^2/6"),
        (3.0, 1.2020569031595943, "zeta(3) (Apery)"),
        (4.0, math.pi**4 / 90, "zeta(4) = pi^4/90"),
    ]:
        print(f"\n  s = {s}   target {name} = {target:.12f}")
        for X in [10, 100, 1000, 10000]:
            val = euler_product(s, X)
            print(f"    X = {X:>6}:  product = {val:.12f}   error = {abs(val - target):.3e}")
    print("\nAn Euler factor exists only because the local series is INFINITE:")
    print("a capacity cliff would truncate it and destroy the identity.")

    rule("Summary")
    print("* P_cure is monotone, always < 1, and tends to 1: a MONOTONE RAMP.")
    print("* Deficiency pinned between p^-k and m p^-k: geometric, never a cliff.")
    print("* P_cure(1) = 1 - 1/p: the first exclusive dimension is NOT sufficient.")
    print("* Marginal gains (p-1) p^-(k+1) strictly decrease: sublinear benefit.")
    print("* Genericity: P_ind(k) = prod_{i<k}(1 - p^{i-n}) >= 1 - (p^k-1)/((p-1)p^n).")
    print("* Joint bound has an interior optimum near k = n/2.")
    print("* Damped failure masses over all characteristics multiply to zeta(s).")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

concept.title: NET-31: Internalization is a seed-fixed trait among cures — same 4 seeds dependent at k=2 and k=3; NET-29's 5/6 was a seed-set-specific high; dependent seeds stay dependent at every width
concept.concept_description:
**Program:** Network/LLM research lab — round-net-31 (mechanism axis; seed-trait-vs-width-trait test). Paper 75. ALL_DONE_NET31, 12 arms.

**Design:** SEED-FIXED, WIDTH-SWEPT freeze. Part A = E=23 (k=3) × seeds 14–19 (7 interventions/arm: ctl/zeroN/zero1@0,1,2/flip1@0/scale0.1); Part B = E=22 (k=2) × seeds 14–19 (6 interventions/arm). The published E=21 (k=1) arms for the same seeds (NET-28 outcomes + NET-29 k=1 zero1 reads) are the k=1 rung, so every seed 14–19 now has internalization reads at k=1/2/3 — seed-fixed, byte-identical EOSWidthGRU, same-seed training, inference-only interventions, fresh eval draws per arm × manipulation.

**Headline law — INTERNALIZATION-IS-A-SEED-FIXED-TRAIT-AMONG-CURES:** the boundary-dependence set is the SAME at k=2 and k=3 — {13, 14, 15, 17} (this round: k=3 zeroN 0.9014/0.7104/0.7437, k=2 0.9141/0.8037/0.9067 for s=14/15/17; s=13 from NET-29/30 = 0.7041/0.7544) — and the same seven seeds are self-sufficient at both widths ⇒ internalization is ~60/40 (7/11 cures) and WIDTH-INDEPENDENT. Width sets P(cure); the seed sets internalization.

**Honest correction:** NET-29's "5/6 self-sufficient at k=3" was a SEED-SET-SPECIFIC HIGH (seeds 8–13: 1/6 dependent; seeds 14–19: 3/6 dependent + 1/6 marginal). Pooled k=3 over seeds 8–19 = 7/12 self-sufficient/marginal.

**Seed-trait confirmed, width-trait refuted:** s=14/15 (the k=1-dependent cures) stay ensemble-dependent at EVERY width and dependence GROWS with k (s=14: −2.8%→−9%→−10%; s=15: −1…−5%→−20%→−29%; s=13: −25%→−30%; s=17: −9%→−26%). But the trait has NO k=1 predictor (s=13 k=1-fail-no-op and s=17 k=1-partial-no-op are dependent at k≥2; s=16/18 k=1-fail-no-ops are self-sufficient) — it only manifests at widths where the seed cures.

**New markers:** (1) k=2 sign-sensitivity = clean dependence marker — flip costs −7 to −25% in 4/4 dependent k=2 arms (sign-opposition required in the two coords) and is flip-free in self-sufficient arms; at k=3 flip = 0% in all 12 arms across both seed sets. (2) NET-29's magnitude→dependence hint REFUTED (self-sufficient s=18 has larger coords than dependent s=14/17). (3) P(cure)=100% at k=3 extends to a SECOND seed set (12/12 merged).

**Mechanism:** at k≥2 the boundary block is used COLLECTIVELY (zero1 = 0% in every arm); dependent seeds gate the answer path on the aggregate block norm (zeroN 9–29%, scale0.1 1–5%).

**Design rule (sharpened):** ≥3 exclusive dims in a final-step boundary token ⇒ reliable training SUCCESS (12/12 cures at k=3, both seed sets), but only ~60% self-sufficient internalization — ~40% of seeds' answer paths lean on the boundary ensemble at eval, so keep re-serving the boundary token or verify internalization per instance.

**Barriers:** (a) clean (new E=22/E=23 solutions with own ctl baselines; k=1 rung = published same-seed arms; inference-only), (b) clean (Catalog no prior), (c) confronted — ≥3 dims = reliable success but ~60% self-sufficient; real-scale remains the frontier, (d) clean, (e) THE round's content (seed-set-heterogeneous rate reported pooled 7/12; the same-4-seeds trait is a within-seed-across-width reproducibility statement), (f) clean (exact writes, SEs, no-op = |Δ|≤1.2 SE), (g) strong (SEED-FIXED design — width the only training variable), (h) design rule + per-instance verification caution.

**Open:** REAL-SCALE transfer (frontier); a trained-WEIGHT predictor of the seed trait; pad384-vs-NET-24-hybrid parity; why dependence grows with k.

# Collective use of a boundary block: the Chinese-Remainder layer

## Context (NET-31, mechanism axis)

The companion file `BoundaryBlockInternalization.lean` models the boundary block
additively: a threshold compared with the aggregate drive `∑ i, w i`.  That layer
explains the sign-sensitivity marker, but it does not explain *why* a block of
`k` exclusive dimensions can carry an answer at all, nor why the round's rule of
thumb is stated in terms of **exclusive** dimensions.

This file supplies the arithmetic layer.  A boundary block of `k` exclusive
dimensions is modelled by `k` **pairwise coprime moduli** `m i ≥ 2`; the answer
path *resolves* a range `A` when the residues `x mod m i`, `i` ranging over the
surviving dimensions, determine `x` on `[0, A)`.  This is the Chinese Remainder
Theorem read as a statement about ablations:

* `BoundaryBlockCRT.resolves_of_le_prod` — the block resolves everything below
  its **capacity** `∏ i ∈ S, m i` (CRT).
* `BoundaryBlockCRT.two_pow_card_le_prod` — `k` exclusive dimensions have
  capacity at least `2 ^ k`; dropping one leaves at least `2 ^ (k-1)`
  (`two_pow_card_sub_one_le_prod_erase`).
* `BoundaryBlockCRT.single_drop_resolves` — hence **`zero1` is a no-op**: with
  `A ≤ 2 ^ (k-1)` every single-dimension ablation still resolves.
* `BoundaryBlockCRT.resolves_empty_iff` — but **`zeroN` is fatal**: with no
  dimensions left the block resolves only ranges with at most one element.
* `BoundaryBlockCRT.collective_use` — the two facts together are precisely the
  round's mechanism claim: *the block is used collectively*.
* `BoundaryBlockCRT.exists_collective_block` — the configuration is realised at
  every width `k ≥ 2` by the Fermat numbers `2 ^ 2 ^ i + 1`, which are pairwise
  coprime, so the mechanism is not an artefact of a lucky modulus choice.
* `BoundaryBlockCRT.single_drop_can_break_without_margin` — an honest boundary:
  the `zero1` no-op needs the capacity margin.  With `(2, 3, 5)` and `A = 30` the
  block resolves, yet dropping the modulus `5` destroys resolution.  So "≥ 3
  exclusive dims" buys redundancy only up to the margin `2 ^ (k-1)`.
* `BoundaryBlockCRT.resolves_neg` — sign flips of a modulus are *always* free at
  this layer.  Sign sensitivity, observed only at `k = 2`, therefore cannot be a
  capacity phenomenon: it belongs to the additive gate layer.
-/

namespace BoundaryBlockCRT

open Finset

variable {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι]

/-- The surviving dimensions `S` of a boundary block with moduli `m` **resolve**
the answer range `A` when residues mod the surviving moduli separate every two
answers in `[0, A)`. -/
def Resolves (S : Finset ι) (m : ι → ℤ) (A : ℤ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : ℤ, 0 ≤ x → x < A → 0 ≤ y → y < A → (∀ i ∈ S, m i ∣ x - y) → x = y

/-- Pairwise coprimality of the surviving moduli. -/
def PairwiseCoprime (S : Finset ι) (m : ι → ℤ) : Prop :=
  (S : Set ι).Pairwise (Function.onFun IsCoprime m)

/-! ## 1.  Capacity: the Chinese Remainder Theorem as an ablation statement -/

omit [DecidableEq ι] in
/-- **CRT.**  A pairwise coprime block resolves every range below its capacity
`∏ i ∈ S, m i`. -/
theorem resolves_of_le_prod {S : Finset ι} {m : ι → ℤ} {A : ℤ}
    (hcop : PairwiseCoprime S m) (hA : A ≤ ∏ i ∈ S, m i) : Resolves S m A := by
  intro x y hx hxA hy hyA hdvd
  have hdvd' : (∏ i ∈ S, m i) ∣ x - y := Finset.prod_dvd_of_coprime hcop hdvd
  have habs : |x - y| < ∏ i ∈ S, m i := by
    rcases abs_cases (x - y) with ⟨h, _⟩ | ⟨h, _⟩ <;> rw [h] <;> linarith
  have := Int.eq_zero_of_abs_lt_dvd hdvd' habs
  linarith

omit [DecidableEq ι] in
/-- `k` exclusive dimensions, each of modulus at least `2`, have capacity at
least `2 ^ k`. -/
theorem two_pow_card_le_prod {S : Finset ι} {m : ι → ℤ} (hm : ∀ i ∈ S, 2 ≤ m i) :
    (2 : ℤ) ^ S.card ≤ ∏ i ∈ S, m i := by
  calc (2 : ℤ) ^ S.card = ∏ _i ∈ S, (2 : ℤ) := by rw [Finset.prod_const]
  _ ≤ ∏ i ∈ S, m i := Finset.prod_le_prod (fun i _ => by norm_num) hm

/-- Dropping one dimension leaves capacity at least `2 ^ (k-1)`. -/
theorem two_pow_card_sub_one_le_prod_erase {S : Finset ι} {m : ι → ℤ} {j : ι}
    (hj : j ∈ S) (hm : ∀ i ∈ S, 2 ≤ m i) :
    (2 : ℤ) ^ (S.card - 1) ≤ ∏ i ∈ S.erase j, m i := by
  have hcard : (S.erase j).card = S.card - 1 := Finset.card_erase_of_mem hj
  have := two_pow_card_le_prod (S := S.erase j) (m := m)
    (fun i hi => hm i (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase hi))
  rwa [hcard] at this

/-! ## 2.  `zero1` is a no-op, `zeroN` is fatal -/

/-- **`zero1` is a no-op.**  With `k` pairwise coprime exclusive dimensions of
modulus `≥ 2` and an answer range within the single-drop margin `2 ^ (k-1)`, the
block still resolves after any one dimension is ablated. -/
theorem single_drop_resolves {S : Finset ι} {m : ι → ℤ} {A : ℤ} {j : ι}
    (hj : j ∈ S) (hm : ∀ i ∈ S, 2 ≤ m i) (hcop : PairwiseCoprime S m)
    (hA : A ≤ (2 : ℤ) ^ (S.card - 1)) : Resolves (S.erase j) m A := by
  refine resolves_of_le_prod ?_ (le_trans hA (two_pow_card_sub_one_le_prod_erase hj hm))
  exact hcop.mono (by
    intro i hi
    exact Finset.mem_of_mem_erase hi)

omit [DecidableEq ι] in
/-- **`zeroN` is fatal.**  With every dimension ablated the block resolves only
degenerate ranges. -/
theorem resolves_empty_iff {m : ι → ℤ} {A : ℤ} :
    Resolves (∅ : Finset ι) m A ↔ A ≤ 1 := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    by_contra hA
    push_neg at hA
    have := h 0 1 le_rfl (by linarith) zero_le_one hA (by simp)
    exact absurd this (by norm_num)
  · intro hA x y hx hxA _ _ _
    omega

/-- **Collective use.**  For a block of `k ≥ 2` pairwise coprime exclusive
dimensions and a non-degenerate answer range inside the single-drop margin: the
intact block resolves, *every* single-dimension ablation is a no-op, and the
whole-block ablation is fatal.  This is the round's mechanism statement. -/
theorem collective_use {S : Finset ι} {m : ι → ℤ} {A : ℤ}
    (hm : ∀ i ∈ S, 2 ≤ m i) (hcop : PairwiseCoprime S m)
    (h2 : 2 ≤ A) (hA : A ≤ (2 : ℤ) ^ (S.card - 1)) :
    Resolves S m A ∧ (∀ j ∈ S, Resolves (S.erase j) m A) ∧ ¬ Resolves (∅ : Finset ι) m A := by
  refine ⟨?_, fun j hj => single_drop_resolves hj hm hcop hA, ?_⟩
  · refine resolves_of_le_prod hcop (le_trans hA ?_)
    refine le_trans (pow_le_pow_right₀ (by norm_num) (Nat.sub_le _ 1)) ?_
    exact two_pow_card_le_prod hm
  · rw [resolves_empty_iff]
    omega

/-! ## 3.  The configuration is realised at every width: Fermat blocks

The Fermat numbers `F i = 2 ^ 2 ^ i + 1` are pairwise coprime and exceed `2`, so
`{F 0, …, F (k-1)}` is a legitimate `k`-dimensional exclusive boundary block for
every `k`.  Nothing about the mechanism depends on a lucky choice of moduli. -/

/-- The Fermat block: `k` pairwise coprime exclusive dimensions. -/
def fermatBlock : ℕ → ℤ := fun i => (Nat.fermatNumber i : ℤ)

theorem two_le_fermatBlock (i : ℕ) : 2 ≤ fermatBlock i := by
  have h : 2 ≤ Nat.fermatNumber i := by
    have : 1 ≤ 2 ^ 2 ^ i := Nat.one_le_two_pow
    simp only [Nat.fermatNumber]
    omega
  unfold fermatBlock
  exact_mod_cast h

theorem pairwiseCoprime_fermatBlock (S : Finset ℕ) : PairwiseCoprime S fermatBlock := by
  intro i _ j _ hij
  have h : Nat.Coprime (Nat.fermatNumber i) (Nat.fermatNumber j) :=
    Nat.coprime_fermatNumber_fermatNumber hij
  exact (Nat.isCoprime_iff_coprime).2 h

/-- **Realisation at every width `k ≥ 2`.**  A genuine `k`-dimensional block,
collectively used: intact resolution, single-drop no-op, whole-block failure. -/
theorem exists_collective_block (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) :
    ∃ (S : Finset ℕ) (m : ℕ → ℤ) (A : ℤ),
      S.card = k ∧ 2 ≤ A ∧
      Resolves S m A ∧ (∀ j ∈ S, Resolves (S.erase j) m A) ∧
      ¬ Resolves (∅ : Finset ℕ) m A := by
  refine ⟨Finset.range k, fermatBlock, (2 : ℤ) ^ (k - 1), Finset.card_range k, ?_, ?_⟩
  · have h1 : 1 ≤ k - 1 := by omega
    calc (2 : ℤ) = 2 ^ 1 := by norm_num
    _ ≤ 2 ^ (k - 1) := pow_le_pow_right₀ (by norm_num) h1
  · have hcard : (Finset.range k).card = k := Finset.card_range k

/-!
# Collective use of a boundary block: the Chinese-Remainder layer

## Context (NET-31, mechanism axis)

The companion file `BoundaryBlockInternalization.lean` models the boundary block
additively: a threshold compared with the aggregate drive `∑ i, w i`.  That layer
explains the sign-sensitivity marker, but it does not explain *why* a block of
`k` exclusive dimensions can carry an answer at all, nor why the round's rule of
thumb is stated in terms of **exclusive** dimensions.

This file supplies the arithmetic layer.  A boundary block of `k` exclusive
dimensions is modelled by `k` **pairwise coprime moduli** `m i ≥ 2`; the answer
path *resolves* a range `A` when the residues `x mod m i`, `i` ranging over the
surviving dimensions, determine `x` on `[0, A)`.  This is the Chinese Remainder
Theorem read as a statement about ablations:

* `BoundaryBlockCRT.resolves_of_le_prod` — the block resolves everything below
  its **capacity** `∏ i ∈ S, m i` (CRT).
* `BoundaryBlockCRT.two_pow_card_le_prod` — `k` exclusive dimensions have
  capacity at least `2 ^ k`; dropping one leaves at least `2 ^ (k-1)`
  (`two_pow_card_sub_one_le_prod_erase`).
* `BoundaryBlockCRT.single_drop_resolves` — hence **`zero1` is a no-op**: with
  `A ≤ 2 ^ (k-1)` every single-dimension ablation still resolves.
* `BoundaryBlockCRT.resolves_empty_iff` — but **`zeroN` is fatal**: with no
  dimensions left the block resolves only ranges with at most one element.
* `BoundaryBlockCRT.collective_use` — the two facts together are precisely the
  round's mechanism claim: *the block is used collectively*.
* `BoundaryBlockCRT.exists_collective_block` — the configuration is realised at
  every width `k ≥ 2` by the Fermat numbers `2 ^ 2 ^ i + 1`, which are pairwise
  coprime, so the mechanism is not an artefact of a lucky modulus choice.
* `BoundaryBlockCRT.single_drop_can_break_without_margin` — an honest boundary:
  the `zero1` no-op needs the capacity margin.  With `(2, 3, 5)` and `A = 30` the
  block resolves, yet dropping the modulus `5` destroys resolution.  So "≥ 3
  exclusive dims" buys redundancy only up to the margin `2 ^ (k-1)`.
* `BoundaryBlockCRT.resolves_neg` — sign flips of a modulus are *always* free at
  this layer.  Sign sensitivity, observed only at `k = 2`, therefore cannot be a
  capacity phenomenon: it belongs to the additive gate layer.
-/

namespace BoundaryBlockCRT

open Finset

variable {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι]

/-- The surviving dimensions `S` of a boundary block with moduli `m` **resolve**
the answer range `A` when residues mod the surviving moduli separate every two
answers in `[0, A)`. -/
def Resolves (S : Finset ι) (m : ι → ℤ) (A : ℤ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : ℤ, 0 ≤ x → x < A → 0 ≤ y → y < A → (∀ i ∈ S, m i ∣ x - y) → x = y

/-- Pairwise coprimality of the surviving moduli. -/
def PairwiseCoprime (S : Finset ι) (m : ι → ℤ) : Prop :=
  (S : Set ι).Pairwise (Function.onFun IsCoprime m)

/-! ## 1.  Capacity: the Chinese Remainder Theorem as an ablation statement -/

omit [DecidableEq ι] in
/-- **CRT.**  A pairwise coprime block resolves every range below its capacity
`∏ i ∈ S, m i`. -/
theorem resolves_of_le_prod {S : Finset ι} {m : ι → ℤ} {A : ℤ}
    (hcop : PairwiseCoprime S m) (hA : A ≤ ∏ i ∈ S, m i) : Resolves S m A := by
  intro x y hx hxA hy hyA hdvd
  have hdvd' : (∏ i ∈ S, m i) ∣ x - y := Finset.prod_dvd_of_coprime hcop hdvd
  have habs : |x - y| < ∏ i ∈ S, m i := by
    rcases abs_cases (x - y) with ⟨h, _⟩ | ⟨h, _⟩ <;> rw [h] <;> linarith
  have := Int.eq_zero_of_abs_lt_dvd hdvd' habs
  linarith

omit [DecidableEq ι] in
/-- `k` exclusive dimensions, each of modulus at least `2`, have capacity at
least `2 ^ k`. -/
theorem two_pow_card_le_prod {S : Finset ι} {m : ι → ℤ} (hm : ∀ i ∈ S, 2 ≤ m i) :
    (2 : ℤ) ^ S.card ≤ ∏ i ∈ S, m i := by
  calc (2 : ℤ) ^ S.card = ∏ _i ∈ S, (2 : ℤ) := by rw [Finset.prod_const]
  _ ≤ ∏ i ∈ S, m i := Finset.prod_le_prod (fun i _ => by norm_num) hm

/-- Dropping one dimension leaves capacity at least `2 ^ (k-1)`. -/
theorem two_pow_card_sub_one_le_prod_erase {S : Finset ι} {m : ι → ℤ} {j : ι}
    (hj : j ∈ S) (hm : ∀ i ∈ S, 2 ≤ m i) :
    (2 : ℤ) ^ (S.card - 1) ≤ ∏ i ∈ S.erase j, m i := by
  have hcard : (S.erase j).card = S.card - 1 := Finset.card_erase_of_mem hj
  have := two_pow_card_le_prod (S := S.erase j) (m := m)
    (fun i hi => hm i (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase hi))
  rwa [hcard] at this

/-! ## 2.  `zero1` is a no-op, `zeroN` is fatal -/

/-- **`zero1` is a no-op.**  With `k` pairwise coprime exclusive dimensions of
modulus `≥ 2` and an answer range within the single-drop margin `2 ^ (k-1)`, the
block still resolves after any one dimension is ablated. -/
theorem single_drop_resolves {S : Finset ι} {m : ι → ℤ} {A : ℤ} {j : ι}
    (hj : j ∈ S) (hm : ∀ i ∈ S, 2 ≤ m i) (hcop : PairwiseCoprime S m)
    (hA : A ≤ (2 : ℤ) ^ (S.card - 1)) : Resolves (S.erase j) m A := by
  refine resolves_of_le_prod ?_ (le_trans hA (two_pow_card_sub_one_le_prod_erase hj hm))
  exact hcop.mono (by
    intro i hi
    exact Finset.mem_of_mem_erase hi)

omit [DecidableEq ι] in
/-- **`zeroN` is fatal.**  With every dimension ablated the block resolves only
degenerate ranges. -/
theorem resolves_empty_iff {m : ι → ℤ} {A : ℤ} :
    Resolves (∅ : Finset ι) m A ↔ A ≤ 1 := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    by_contra hA
    push_neg at hA
    have := h 0 1 le_rfl (by linarith) zero_le_one hA (by simp)
    exact absurd this (by norm_num)
  · intro hA x y hx hxA _ _ _
    omega

/-- **Collective use.**  For a block of `k ≥ 2` pairwise coprime exclusive
dimensions and a non-degenerate answer range inside the single-drop margin: the
intact block resolves, *every* single-dimension ablation is a no-op, and the
whole-block ablation is fatal.  This is the round's mechanism statement. -/
theorem collective_use {S : Finset ι} {m : ι → ℤ} {A : ℤ}
    (hm : ∀ i ∈ S, 2 ≤ m i) (hcop : PairwiseCoprime S m)
    (h2 : 2 ≤ A) (hA : A ≤ (2 : ℤ) ^ (S.card - 1)) :
    Resolves S m A ∧ (∀ j ∈ S, Resolves (S.erase j) m A) ∧ ¬ Resolves (∅ : Finset ι) m A := by
  refine ⟨?_, fun j hj => single_drop_resolves hj hm hcop hA, ?_⟩
  · refine resolves_of_le_prod hcop (le_trans hA ?_)
    refine le_trans (pow_le_pow_right₀ (by norm_num) (Nat.sub_le _ 1)) ?_
    exact two_pow_card_le_prod hm
  · rw [resolves_empty_iff]
    omega

/-! ## 3.  The configuration is realised at every width: Fermat blocks

The Fermat numbers `F i = 2 ^ 2 ^ i + 1` are pairwise coprime and exceed `2`, so
`{F 0, …, F (k-1)}` is a legitimate `k`-dimensional exclusive boundary block for
every `k`.  Nothing about the mechanism depends on a lucky choice of moduli. -/

/-- The Fermat block: `k` pairwise coprime exclusive dimensions. -/
def fermatBlock : ℕ → ℤ := fun i => (Nat.fermatNumber i : ℤ)

theorem two_le_fermatBlock (i : ℕ) : 2 ≤ fermatBlock i := by
  have h : 2 ≤ Nat.fermatNumber i := by
    have : 1 ≤ 2 ^ 2 ^ i := Nat.one_le_two_pow
    simp only [Nat.fermatNumber]
    omega
  unfold fermatBlock
  exact_mod_cast h

theorem pairwiseCoprime_fermatBlock (S : Finset ℕ) : PairwiseCoprime S fermatBlock := by
  intro i _ j _ hij
  have h : Nat.Coprime (Nat.fermatNumber i) (Nat.fermatNumber j) :=
    Nat.coprime_fermatNumber_fermatNumber hij
  exact (Nat.isCoprime_iff_coprime).2 h

/-- **Realisation at every width `k ≥ 2`.**  A genuine `k`-dimensional block,
collectively used: intact resolution, single-drop no-op, whole-block failure. -/
theorem exists_collective_block (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) :
    ∃ (S : Finset ℕ) (m : ℕ → ℤ) (A : ℤ),
      S.card = k ∧ 2 ≤ A ∧
      Resolves S m A ∧ (∀ j ∈ S, Resolves (S.erase j) m A) ∧
      ¬ Resolves (∅ : Finset ℕ) m A := by
  refine ⟨Finset.range k, fermatBlock, (2 : ℤ) ^ (k - 1), Finset.card_range k, ?_, ?_⟩
  · have h1 : 1 ≤ k - 1 := by omega
    calc (2 : ℤ) = 2 ^ 1 := by norm_num
    _ ≤ 2 ^ (k - 1) := pow_le_pow_right₀ (by norm_num) h1
  · have hcard : (Finset.range k).card = k := Finset.card_range k
    have h2 : (2 : ℤ) ≤ (2 : ℤ) ^ (k - 1) := by
      have h1 : 1 ≤ k - 1 := by omega
      calc (2 : ℤ) = 2 ^ 1 := by norm_num
      _ ≤ 2 ^ (k - 1) := pow_le_pow_right₀ (by norm_num) h1
    have := collective_use (S := Finset.range k) (m := fermatBlock) (A := (2 : ℤ) ^ (k - 1))
      (fun i _ => two_le_fermatBlock i) (pairwiseCoprime_fermatBlock _) h2
      (by rw [hcard])
    exact this

/-! ## 4.  Honest boundaries -/

/-- **The `zero1` no-op needs the margin.**  The block `(2, 3, 5)` resolves the
range `30`, but ablating the dimension `5` destroys resolution (`0` and `6` become
indistinguishable).  Redundancy of `k ≥ 3` exclusive dimensions is therefore a
statement *relative to the answer range*, exactly as the design rule's
per-instance verification caveat demands. -/
theorem single_drop_can_break_without_margin :
    ∃ (S : Finset ℕ) (m : ℕ → ℤ) (A : ℤ) (j : ℕ),
      PairwiseCoprime S m ∧ j ∈ S ∧ Resolves S m A ∧ ¬ Resolves (S.erase j) m A := by
  classical
  refine ⟨{0, 1, 2}, fun i => if i = 0 then 2 else if i = 1 then 3 else 5, 30, 2, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro i hi j hj hij
    simp only [Finset.coe_insert, Set.mem_insert_iff, Finset.coe_singleton,
      Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hi hj
    rcases hi with rfl | rfl | rfl <;> rcases hj with rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
      simp_all [Function.onFun, Int.isCoprime_iff_gcd_eq_one] <;> decide
  · decide
  · refine resolves_of_le_prod ?_ ?_
    · intro i hi j hj hij
      simp only [Finset.coe_insert, Set.mem_insert_iff, Finset.coe_singleton,
        Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hi hj
      rcases hi with rfl | rfl | rfl <;> rcases hj with rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
        simp_all [Function.onFun, Int.isCoprime_iff_gcd_eq_one] <;> decide
    · decide
  · intro h
    have h6 : (0 : ℤ) = 6 := by
      refine h 0 6 le_rfl (by norm_num) (by norm_num) (by norm_num) ?_
      intro i hi
      fin_cases hi <;> norm_num
    norm_num at h6

/-- **Sign flips are free at the capacity layer.**  Negating any subset of the
moduli changes nothing, because divisibility is sign-blind.  The `k = 2` sign
sensitivity found in the round is therefore *not* a capacity effect: it lives in
the additive gate (`BoundaryBlockInternalization.flip1_breaks_of_width_two`). -/
theorem resolves_neg {S : Finset ι} {m : ι → ℤ} {A : ℤ} (T : Finset ι) :
    Resolves S (fun i => if i ∈ T then -(m i) else m i) A ↔ Resolves S m A := by
  constructor <;> intro h x y hx hxA hy hyA hdvd <;>
    refine h x y hx hxA hy hyA (fun i hi => ?_)
  · by_cases hiT : i ∈ T <;> simp [hiT, (neg_dvd).2 (hdvd i hi), hdvd i hi]
  · have := hdvd i hi
    by_cases hiT : i ∈ T
    · simpa [hiT, neg_dvd] using this
    · simpa [hiT] using this

end BoundaryBlockCRT
